record.paper_title: Recent developments and open problems in the theory of permanents
record.original_question: Can one give a unifying explanation for the similarities between matrix positivity as a positive-semidefinite operator condition, meaning a Hermitian matrix A with x*Ax >= 0 for every vector x, and entrywise positivity or nonnegativity, especially for permanent inequalities and related matrix properties?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Olga Taussky observed that a number of theorems valid for Hermitian positive semidefinite matrices (Hermitian matrices $A$ satisfying $x^{*}Ax \ge 0$ for every vector $x$) have close analogues that hold for matrices whose entries (or whose minors of all orders) are nonnegative, but that the known proofs in the two settings are typically different. Examples of this parallel include the nonnegativity of eigenvalues, monotonicity properties of eigenvalues under principal submatrix extraction, the positivity of principal minors, and various permanent inequalities (such as inequalities of Schur, Marcus, and Lieb type), all of which are known for both positive semidefinite Hermitian matrices and for entrywise/totally nonnegative matrices.

Problem. Provide a single unified mathematical framework that explains, in a rigorous way, the parallel between the following two notions of "positivity" for a square matrix $A$ with complex entries:
(i) operator positivity: $A$ is Hermitian and $x^{*}Ax \ge 0$ for all vectors $x$;
(ii) entrywise positivity / total nonnegativity: every entry of $A$ (respectively every minor of $A$) is nonnegative.

More precisely, identify a common structural principle (for instance a common axiomatic class of matrices, a common cone-theoretic or representation-theoretic mechanism, or a common proof technique) from which the shared theorems — in particular the parallel permanent inequalities and the shared spectral and minor-positivity properties — can be deduced simultaneously for both classes.
artifact.status_search_result: The Taussky unification problem, posed by Olga Taussky in 1958, asks for a unified treatment of theorems shared by positive semidefinite Hermitian matrices and entrywise/totally nonnegative matrices. Subsequent work (e.g., on M-matrices, totally nonnegative matrices, and structured matrices) has clarified partial common features (positivity of principal minors, eigenvalue monotonicity, weak sign symmetry), but no single overarching unifying framework is generally accepted, and the problem is regarded as broadly open with various partial answers.

status_evidence.title: Olga, matrix theory and the Taussky unification problem
status_evidence.snippet: Taussky pointed out in 1958 that similar theorems were known for some positive matrices and for positive definite Hermitian matrices ... and asked for a unified treatment of both cases.
status_evidence.claim: The problem was explicitly posed by Taussky and remains a guiding question with only partial answers.

status_evidence.title: Olga Taussky-Todd's Influence on Matrix Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Hermitian positive definite, nonsingular totally nonnegative, and M-matrices all enjoy positivity of principal minors, weak sign symmetry, and eigenvalue monotonicity.
status_evidence.claim: Partial unifications via shared properties of structured matrix classes are known but not a complete unification.

status_evidence.title: Theorems and counterexamples on structured matrices
status_evidence.snippet: The term 'Taussky unification problem' was later taken to mean a much wider class of problems.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is regarded as broad and still actively investigated.
